brief: 6 startup mistakes every second-time founder never makes again.

slots.subtitle: The expensive lessons learned by founders who have survived the first crucible and refuse to repeat them.

slots.title: BUILD FOR
slots.subtitle: The first-time founder falls in love with a solution; the second falls in love with a problem.
slots.bodyText: We spent six months building features nobody asked for. Now we run discovery calls before we write a single line of code. Validation is cheaper than engineering.
slots.calloutBody: Fall in love with the problem, not the solution.

slots.title: HIRE
slots.subtitle: A bad hire costs more than an empty seat; culture is not a poster on the wall.
slots.bodyText: We used to hire for velocity and regret it later. Now we hire for values alignment and verify with paid trials. One exceptional operator beats five mediocre ones.
slots.calloutBody: Culture is who you hire, fire, and promote.

slots.title: WATCH
slots.subtitle: Second-time founders treat cash like oxygen: they know exactly how much remains and when the tank runs empty.
slots.bodyText: We used to celebrate fundraising as a finish line. Now we treat it as fuel with a countdown. Unit economics come before growth hacks every single time.
slots.calloutBody: Revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, but cash is king.

slots.title: SHIP
slots.subtitle: Perfection is the enemy of learning; the best founders launch ugly and iterate with their earliest believers.
slots.bodyText: We waited a year for the perfect product and launched to silence. Now we ship in weeks and let user feedback drive the roadmap. Done beats perfect.
slots.calloutBody: If you are not embarrassed by your first version, you shipped too late.

slots.title: OWN
slots.subtitle: The founder who does every job becomes the bottleneck; smart founders build systems that outlast their own calendar.
slots.bodyText: I used to believe nobody could do it as well as me. Now I hire for ownership and document every decision. Your job is to build the machine, not crank the handle.
slots.calloutBody: Build systems that make you replaceable.

slots.title: KEEP
slots.subtitle: First-time founders chase new logos; veterans obsess over the ones who stay, expand, and advocate without asking.
slots.bodyText: We used to pour capital into acquisition while churn quietly bled us dry. Now we measure net revenue retention before CAC. Retention is the only growth hack that compounds.
slots.calloutBody: You cannot grow your way out of a leaky bucket.

slots.ctaBody: Pick one mistake to eliminate this quarter and watch your runway extend overnight.
